items.markingKey: (b) Start of the Chipko movement (1973); Start of the Appiko movement (1983); The Brundtland Report "Our Common Future" (1987); The Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro (1992).
options: The Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Black soil, also called regur, is best suited for growing cotton.
Reason (R): Most of the water on the Earth is glacier water found in the oceans.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Most of the water on the Earth is salt water found in the oceans.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) "A thing becomes a resource only when people find a use for it." Explain with examples. (3 marks)
(b) Why are coal and petroleum called non-renewable resources? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Value comes from usefulness and the technology to use it. (2) Uranium became valuable only after nuclear technology developed. (3) Sunlight became a source of electricity with solar panels. (b) (1) They take millions of years to form. (2) Their stock is limited and is used up much faster than it can be replaced.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Value comes from usefulness and the technology to use it. (2) Uranium became valuable only after nuclear technology developed. (3) Sunlight became a source of electricity with solar panels. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) They take millions of years to form. (2) Their stock is limited and is used up much faster than it can be replaced.

items.stem: What is meant by 'open-cast mining'?
items.answer: Extraction of minerals by removing the surface layers of land, leaving large pits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: extraction of minerals by removing the surface layers of land, leaving large pits.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 8 student on "Conservation and sustainable development of resources" and answer the questions that follow.
"In the Chipko movement, villagers (A) ______ trees to stop them from being cut. The Chipko movement began in the 1970s in the hills of present-day (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is conservation of resources necessary? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) hugged (ii) Uttarakhand (iii) (1) Many resources are limited and can run out. (2) Careless use damages the environment for future generations.
items.markingKey: (i) hugged – 1 mark. (ii) Uttarakhand – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Many resources are limited and can run out. (2) Careless use damages the environment for future generations.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'biotic resources'?
items.answer: Resources obtained from living things, such as plants, animals and fish
items.markingKey: (b) 'Biotic resources' means resources obtained from living things, such as plants, animals and fish; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Large-scale cutting of forests for farming, mining, roads or timber
Resources obtained from living things, such as plants, animals and fish
Fertile soil deposited by rivers, the most widespread soil of the northern plains of India
Resources obtained from non-living things, such as rocks, minerals and air

items.stem: Which of the following is a cause of deforestation?
items.answer: Mining
items.markingKey: (a) Mining is a cause of deforestation; Social forestry, Protecting sacred groves, Declaring a national park are not.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Fossil fuels such as coal were formed from buried plant and animal remains over tens of years.
Reason (R): Buildings, roads and machines are human-made resources.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Fossil fuels such as coal were formed from buried plant and animal remains over millions of years. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: About ______ of the Earth's surface is covered by water.
items.answer: three-fourths
items.markingKey: (c) About three-fourths of the Earth's surface is covered by water.

items.stem:
(a) Only a small share of the Earth's water can be used by people. Explain why, and what this means for India. (3 marks)
(b) Why is land called the most important natural resource for people? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Most water is salty ocean water. (2) Much fresh water is locked in ice caps and glaciers. (3) Usable fresh water in rivers, lakes and groundwater is small. (4) India has a large population and uneven rainfall, so water must be used carefully. (b) (1) It supports farming, forests and animals. (2) People build houses, industries and roads on it.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Most water is salty ocean water. (2) Much fresh water is locked in ice caps and glaciers. (3) Usable fresh water in rivers, lakes and groundwater is small. (4) India has a large population and uneven rainfall, so water must be used carefully. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) It supports farming, forests and animals. (2) People build houses, industries and roads on it.

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Rainwater harvesting
2. Abiotic resources
3. Groundwater depletion
4. Conservation
Column B:
(p) Collecting and storing rainwater from rooftops or land for later use
(q) Resources obtained from non-living things, such as rocks, minerals and air
(r) Fall of the water table when wells pump out more water than rain recharges
(s) Careful and planned use of resources to prevent waste and damage
items.markingKey: (a) Rainwater harvesting – collecting and storing rainwater from rooftops or land for later use; Abiotic resources – resources obtained from non-living things, such as rocks, minerals and air; Groundwater depletion – fall of the water table when wells pump out more water than rain recharges; Conservation – careful and planned use of resources to prevent waste and damage.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: Burning of coal and petroleum adds nitrogen to the atmosphere.
items.answer: False. Burning of coal and petroleum adds carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: 'carbon dioxide' in place of 'nitrogen' (½ mark). Burning of coal and petroleum adds carbon dioxide to the atmosphere.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Black soil is ideal for cotton cultivation.
Reason (R): Black soil has a high capacity to hold moisture.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Moisture retention is the main reason black soil suits cotton.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False: Amrita Devi and other Bishnois gave their lives in 1730 to protect khejri trees at Khejarli in Rajasthan.
items.answer: True
items.markingKey: True. Amrita Devi and other Bishnois gave their lives in 1730 to protect khejri trees at Khejarli in Rajasthan.

items.stem:
(a) "Overuse of resources by one generation is unfair to the next." Do you agree? Give reasons. (3 marks)
(b) Give two effects of deforestation. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Non-renewable stocks once used cannot be replaced. (2) Damaged forests, soils and rivers take decades to recover. (3) Future generations will face shortages and higher costs. (b) (1) Soil erosion and floods increase. (2) Wild animals lose their habitat.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Non-renewable stocks once used cannot be replaced. (2) Damaged forests, soils and rivers take decades to recover. (3) Future generations will face shortages and higher costs. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Soil erosion and floods increase. (2) Wild animals lose their habitat.

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Human resource
2. Abiotic resources
3. Conservation
4. Laterite soil
Column B:
(p) Soil formed in areas of heavy rainfall where nutrients are washed away by leaching
(q) People with their knowledge, skills and health, who turn nature's materials into useful things
(r) Resources obtained from non-living things, such as rocks, minerals and air
(s) Careful and planned use of resources to prevent waste and damage
items.markingKey: (c) Human resource – people with their knowledge, skills and health, who turn nature's materials into useful things; Abiotic resources – resources obtained from non-living things, such as rocks, minerals and air; Conservation – careful and planned use of resources to prevent waste and damage; Laterite soil – soil formed in areas of heavy rainfall where nutrients are washed away by leaching.

items.stem: What is meant by 'recycling'?
items.answer: Processing used materials such as paper or metal so that they can be made into new products.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: processing used materials such as paper or metal so that they can be made into new products.

items.stem: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
items.answer: Tidal energy
items.markingKey: (a) Tidal energy is a renewable resource; Natural gas, Coal, Iron ore are not.
